headword: {勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}
gloss: rewarding good and punishing evil; poetic justice

definitions.gloss: rewarding good and punishing evil; poetic justice
definitions.explanation: A moral principle and narrative theme in which good deeds are rewarded and evil deeds are punished. Commonly used to describe stories, dramas, and cultural works that follow this clear-cut moral framework.

examples.english: A story of good triumphing over evil.

notes:
A four-character compound (⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧): {勧|かん} (encourage) + ⟦{善|ぜん}→善：00465_zen⟧ (good) + {懲|ちょう} (punish) + {悪|あく} (evil). This is one of the foundational moral themes in East Asian literature and drama.

CULTURAL NOTE:
This concept is central to traditional Japanese storytelling. Period dramas (⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧) like {水戸黄門|みとこうもん} and {遠山|とおやま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{金|きん}さん are classic examples — the hero always defeats the villain and justice prevails. Modern usage sometimes carries a slightly dismissive tone, implying the story is simplistic or predictable.
